fields.meta_title: 404 Page Examples and Best Practices | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A 404 page tells visitors a URL doesn't exist. See 404 page examples by site type and the status code rules, then build yours from a prompt.
fields.h1: Build a 404 Page That Finds the Next Page
fields.hero_description: Describe your site and Emergent builds the 404 page behind it, with search over your own content and a table of every URL that missed.
fields.features_subheading: Describe the site once and Emergent writes the page, the data behind it and the code you keep.
fields.feature_1:
A status code you ask for by name

Your prompt asks for every unknown URL to answer with a 404 and the designed page. Crawlers read the code; people read the page. Step 6 of the how-to shows how to confirm it.
fields.feature_2:
Search over your own pages

A search box on the error page queries your own products or docs. Words from the broken URL prefill the box, and a visitor who mistyped a single letter is one click away.
fields.feature_3:
Every miss saved as a row

Each missed URL lands as a row in a database you own, the same one behind your app. Query it any time or connect it to tools your team already uses, with no outside analytics script.
fields.feature_4:
Your own navigation and footer

Your site navigation and footer stay on the error page, in your own fonts and colors. Visitors can tell they never left, and the menu they already know stays one glance away.
fields.feature_5:
Copy in the voice you describe

Emergent writes the heading and the next-step links in the voice your prompt sets out. Describe that voice in a sentence, then edit any line of it before the page goes live.
fields.feature_6:
Code you keep

The 404 page and its miss log export to your GitHub repository. Host them on Emergent under your custom domain, or deploy the code wherever the rest of your site already runs.

fields.usecase_heading: 404 Pages for Four Kinds of Site
fields.tab_content_1:
A dead product link that still sells

A shopper who follows an old link to Northwind's retired linen camp shirt lands on a page that keeps the store open. Search sits at the top, with the store's bestsellers below it and an add-to-cart button on each. An add from the error page is saved with the missed URL attached.
fields.tab_content_2:
Search seeded from the broken URL

Acme's API docs collect mistyped links from forum posts and old emails. When /docs/api/webhoks misses, the 404 splits the path into words and searches the docs. The closest article comes first: Webhooks: retries and signatures. A link to the docs home and a support email sit under the result.
fields.tab_content_3:
Let the joke carry a link back to the work

Fernhill is a design studio, and its visitors come to see projects. Its 404 opens with one line, "This page is out sketching," and one button, Show me a random project, that loads a case study from the portfolio. A plain homepage link sits under the button for anyone who wants the full menu.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which old URLs need a redirect this week

Site migrations leave old addresses alive in newsletters and other people's posts. After Globex moved its marketing site, each 404 hit lands in a table with the URL, the referrer and a seven-day count. Every Monday, a Slack post to the web team lists the URLs with 20 or more hits as candidates for a 301 redirect.

fields.howto_description: A 404 page has one job: send someone who hit a dead address to the next page worth opening. Emergent builds it from a description of your site.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Find where your misses come from
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the heading in plain words
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the source of your broken links: retired products, mistyped docs URLs or addresses from an old site. The source decides what the page leads with: a search box for typos, products for a store, a pointer for a move.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Admit the miss in one short heading, then name the likely cause, such as an outdated link, without blaming the visitor. Keep the error code in small type below it; the heading and the next step do the work.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Under whatever leads the page, add two or three plain links: the homepage, your most visited section and a way to contact you.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the error page lean. Drop pop-ups and sign-up forms that compete with the way out. Click every link on it before launch, because a 404 page with a broken link of its own sends visitors in a circle.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Save each 404 hit with the requested URL and its referrer. The referrer column tells a one-off typo apart from a partner site whose broken link sends you traffic every day.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Check the status code before launch
fields.howto_step_6_des: Request an address that never existed and read the response in your browser's network tab. It should say 404. A 200 on an error page is a soft 404, and Google keeps it out of Search.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sort the miss log by hits once a week. A URL whose content moved gets a 301 to its new address. For a page you removed on purpose, answer with 410 Gone, which MDN defines as a permanent removal. Check the list again after any release that renames pages.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits into galleries (404s.design, Dribbble, Awwwards, a Reddit thread) and definitions (Wikipedia, MDN, Mailchimp, USWDS). None of them builds the page or covers what happens after a visitor hits it. This page answers the definition up top for the AI Overview, gives the status-code rules from Google and MDN that the galleries skip, and shows four real 404 pages by site type, including one that turns every missed URL into a row so the broken links get fixed.

claims_to_source: A 404 status says the server cannot find the resource, without saying whether the absence is temporary or permanent; 410 Gone marks a permanent removal
A soft 404 is an error page that returns a 200 status, and Google excludes it from Search
Google does not index URLs that return 4xx codes and removes ones already indexed
A page that moved should return a 301 permanent redirect to its new URL
404 errors on URLs that never existed or were removed do not hurt how the rest of a site ranks
Government guidance for 404 pages: plain, non-technical language, a search bar, next steps, no whimsy where users need critical services
GitHub Pages serves a 404.html file at the root of the repository as the site's custom 404 page
Search Console's Page Indexing report lists URLs that returned Not found (404)

findings.fix: 'Deploy the code with the rest of your site, or host the whole site on Emergent under your custom domain.'

findings.quote: FAQ 3: 'Someone mistyped it, the page was deleted, or it moved without a redirect while old links kept the old address.'; FAQ 6: 'whatever loads is that site's 404 page'
findings.issue: FAQ 3's list of causes has no domain_sources entry, though it is common knowledge and in line with MDN's 'broken or dead links'. FAQ 6 is not always true: a site that redirects misses to its homepage shows a soft 404, which step 6 itself warns about.
findings.fix: FAQ 6: add 'unless the site redirects every miss to its homepage, which is a soft 404'.

findings.quote: An add from the error page is saved with the missed URL attached.
findings.issue: 'An add' as a noun reads as shorthand, not as something a product lead would say aloud.
findings.fix: 'Each add to cart from the error page is saved with the missed URL.'
